conclusions.question: Why did the two P2 sources time out?
conclusions.verified: B and C exhausted the instrumented AP limit (~3592s); B wrapper exited0 after reporting TIMEOUT, C Job returned124. Both lack final valid C,w.
conclusions.inference: Job CPU/wall ~0.965 and ~0.978 is consistent with expensive active computation, not a mostly idle worker.
conclusions.unknown: Exact late-stage cause, completed precision rows and remaining work; timeout is not mathematical impossibility.
conclusions.proposed: Obtain valid full-duration observations before attributing delay or predicting runtime.

conclusions.question: Were the failed probes making numerical progress?
conclusions.verified: Their first ~10s profiles record original _row/_sectors and exp/sqrt arithmetic; Job CPU accumulated for most of the run.
conclusions.inference: They entered genuine AP computation; aggregate CPU is not proof of later precision/eigenvalue convergence.
conclusions.unknown: Progress after the first profile dump; no rank/C/w milestones survive.
conclusions.proposed: Original-operation stage/precision milestones and independent CPU/working-set samples, approval required.
conclusions.evidence: profiles and dummy reproduction; full_support_c4_worker.py main/_row

conclusions.question: Which stage is the primary bottleneck?
conclusions.verified: All retained target profiles stop at initial sector construction; dump_stats calls create_stats which disables the profiler, reproduced on dummy work.
conclusions.inference: exp/sqrt dominate only the captured startup interval; spectral/LU/matrix stages are static cost candidates, not measured bottlenecks.
conclusions.proposed: Approve minimal observer correction; never substitute formulas/precision or claim eighe is the measured bottleneck.

conclusions.question: Resource exhaustion, suspension or numerical difficulty?
conclusions.verified: A has15.578s watchdog gap/AC0 and safety Job125; B/C recorded float64 gate rejection with tiny negative eigenvalues. C AC1/no recorded gap; B has no power watch.
conclusions.inference: Gate rejection explains why original AP fallback is required; it does not quantify physical AP conditioning or prove singularity.
conclusions.unknown: No RSS/commit/page-fault time series, AP eigenspectrum or OS suspend event record; no supported OOM/stall diagnosis.
conclusions.proposed: Retain safety stop classification and add approved nonnumerical resource telemetry.

conclusions.question: Can operational improvements reduce runtime?
conclusions.verified: Collector loses profiling after its first dump; redundant preflight gate and unused MI-noise allocation exist outside source evaluation. No timing establishes their material overhead.
conclusions.inference: Stable AC and valid observability can prevent wasted interruptions; speedup of the mathematical worker is unmeasured.
conclusions.unknown: Magnitude of profiling overhead or setup savings; no promised runtime reduction.
conclusions.proposed: Approve observer/ledger improvements separately; do not replace LU, precision, quadrature, backend or scientific operations.
conclusions.evidence: probe_worker; ExactMBEvaluator.__init__; profile_worker; local mpmath linalg.py
